scope: Add the fastest standards-correct Matroska MPEG-4 Part 2/MP3 to AVI path as a bounded packet-copy route instead of decoding and re-encoding compatible streams.

smallBrowserValidation.command: npx playwright test --grep "genuine AVI|AVI stream copy" --workers=1
assertions: output begins with RIFF and AVI form signatures and probes as genuine AVI
MPEG-4 Part 2 video and both single- and multi-track MP3 packets equal their Matroska sources
output video fully decodes and matches the decoded source
general title/comment and stream titles are retained while language, dispositions, subtitles, attachments, and chapters are explicitly excluded
injected bounded destination-write failure reaches the UI and deletes the partial output
terminal pending operations and queued bytes are zero

buildValidation.isolatedCandidateOutcome: The exact pinned no-Docker build compiled successfully; only within-remux.wasm differed while its loader and manifest were byte-identical.
buildValidation.firstAllCoreReproductionOutcome: The bounded AVI core reproduced exactly, but the first all-core run proved the AVI muxer patch had also changed five unrelated specialist Wasm modules.
buildValidation.isolationResolution: Both build paths now retain the bounded AVI library for within-remux only, reverse the AVI patch, and reinstall stock libavformat before linking any already-certified specialist core.
buildValidation.exactReproductionResult: pending after the implementation checkpoint is pushed

harnessCorrection.firstStressAttempt: The browser conversion, cancellation, and independent packet/decode work were valid, but a newly added validator accidentally applied the OGV format assertion to AVI.
harnessCorrection.resolution: The validator now keeps the Ogg and AVI signature assertions independent; no converter code, memory threshold, packet check, or cleanup rule changed.
harnessCorrection.firstFieldAttempt: The validator assumed AVI would drop stream titles, but the browser output proved that FFmpeg stores and recovers all three titles.
harnessCorrection.fieldResolution: The accepted field contract now requires general title/comment and stream-title retention while asserting the observed loss of language and default-disposition fields.
